title: BART recovered payroll money through diversion while the pension stayed intact

beats.text: How did one BART payroll investigation end in three different outcomes?

visual.sub: The inspector substantiated pay for substantial time away from duty

beats.text: The employee claimed 27 workdays in a 29-day span.

visual.label: The inspector substantiated pay for substantial time away from duty

beats.text: BART’s inspector substantiated pay for substantial time away from duty.

visual.kicker: The inspector substantiated pay for substantial time away from duty

beats.text: A supervisor had adjusted time records. BART investigated separately.
The supervisor retired on April 30 after receiving a notice of termination.

visual.kicker: The supervisor’s personnel proceeding followed a separate track

beats.text: In June 2024, BART reported monthly restitution through a diversion program.

visual.kicker: Restitution moved forward without a criminal conviction

beats.text: The report gave no total amount paid or still due.
The prosecutor declined to pursue criminal charges.
CalPERS could not make the requested reduction to the pension.

visual.kicker: The pension recommendation closed without a reduction

beats.text: In 2026, all three recommendations showed implemented.
One status covered different results for pay, pensions, and personnel.
Every source is linked in the case file below.

chapters.p: The inspector substantiated pay for substantial time away from duty
chapters.b: The supervisor’s personnel proceeding followed a separate track
chapters.o: The pension recommendation closed without a reduction
